text.tspan: Two-way traffic with option 3: each side needs its OWN way out (private NAT) and its OWN way in (NLB)
Why one NAT can't carry both directions
A NAT translates only connections that START inside it (it
remembers them, like conntrack). A packet that arrives at 10.100.0.5
with no matching connection has no pod to go to, so it's dropped.
AWS NAT gateways never forward ports inward: the way in is an NLB.
Lattice: built in. Each side publishes services in the same service network.
PrivateLink: one endpoint service per direction (mirror the setup).
Re-IP or IPv6: normal routing both ways; security groups decide.
Replies never need extra setup: they follow the existing connection.
